headline: No school changed tier this run; Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and the University of South Florida remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-approved CPT. The CPT lawsuit (AAU et al. v. DHS et al., No. 1:26-cv-14520, D. Mass.) remains pending with no ruling; a fresh search again found no independent corroboration of the Nov. 6 hearing date reported only on Carnegie Mellon's own page. Guidance remains in effect.

tripwires.name: DHS SEVIS Help Hub CPT page
tripwires.detail: Direct fetch succeeded again 16 Oct 18:16 UTC (17 Oct 02:16 HKT). Page unchanged, still "Last Updated: August 24, 2026"; cancellation section still only permits cancelling CPT before its start date and, after the start date, only editing the authorisation to shorten the end date — not cancel it outright. No mention of the 5 Oct lawsuit. No change to the page itself.

tripwires.name: Tufts I-Center CPT page
tripwires.detail: Direct fetch succeeded again 16 Oct 18:16 UTC — the "the I-Center is unable to process CPT requests for non-required internships at this time" sentence is still present, unchanged; still nothing either way about students who already hold CPT authorisation. No change detected.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: Checked 16 Oct 18:16 UTC — DHS's own CPT-guidance tripwire page re-confirmed via direct fetch, unchanged: still only says SEVP 'plans to release draft guidance' clarifying prior CPT documents, no date given. A general Federal Register search again found no CPT-specific rulemaking, only secondary law-firm summaries of the August broadcast messages. Lawsuit: one law-firm piece now states the government's response to the preliminary-injunction motion is due 19 Oct per the public docket, unverified against the docket itself; no hearing date, order or ruling found independent of Carnegie Mellon's own page. CPT remains guidance, not a rule.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Still tripped, re-checked 16 Oct 18:16 UTC — no school newly moved into 'cancels' this run. Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and University of South Florida remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-granted CPT.

tiers.label: Already-approved CPT stopped or withdrawn
tiers.sub: The most severe response: students who already held an authorisation were told to stop work, or had it withdrawn.

context: First CPT-specific litigation: on 5 Oct a coalition (AAU, Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, NAFSA, AICUM) sued DHS in federal court in Massachusetts over the Aug 12/24 BCMs, calling them procedurally invalid and impermissibly retroactive, with an emergency injunction motion filed the same night seeking to block enforcement while the case proceeds; case is Association of American Universities et al. v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security et al., No. 1:26-cv-14520 (D. Mass.); pending, no ruling yet (NAFSA held a member town hall on the case 7 Oct). No third broadcast message. DHS's stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the new standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.
